To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we present a new approach for the SAR imaging problem that is based on a novel optimization formulation and a new algorithm that can handle complex-valued images and can be applied to real SAR data.

(1) We derive the proximal operators for the complex valued SAR imaging problem, (2) We show that ADMM is a very efficient algorithm for the SAR imaging problem with complex valued data, and (3) We demonstrate the effectiveness of the ADMM algorithm with complex valued data for real data.

we present a solution for complex valued SAR imaging within a constrained optimization framework, where the objective function combines the $\ell _ 1$-norm of the reflectivity and its magnitude-total-variation, and we provide rigorous derivation of the proximal mapping operator for the magnitude-total-variation of complex valued images.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of new techniques for the solution of SAR imaging problems based on the use of the $\ell_1$-norm of the magnitude of complex valued reflectivity and total-variation of the magnitude of reflectivity.
the development of new methods for complex-valued compressed radar imaging, based on recent advances in signal processing.
the development of an efficient algorithm for SAR imaging that exploits the sparsity of the complex-valued SAR data and the piecewise-constant nature of the magnitude of SAR images.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presented method is able to provide high-quality complex-valued SAR imaging results with high computational efficiency.
the proposed algorithm provides a computationally efficient solution for complex-valued reflectivity SAR image reconstruction with multiple features.
the proposed algorithm can be used to reconstruct the complex SAR image from the undersampled data, which can be used to obtain the real and imaginary part of the complex image.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have presented a novel method for SAR imaging based on the Alternating Directions Method of Multipliers, which can handle complex-valued data.

we have proposed a new algorithm for complex valued SAR imaging based on the Alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) and we have derived the proximal operators for complex valued SAR images.
we present a novel method to solve complex valued SAR imaging problem using a constrained optimization formulation.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the ADMM technique is well suited for complex valued SAR image reconstruction problems, and that the proposed algorithm is able to reconstruct images with multiple features, including piecewise constant features.
, by using complex-valued data, we obtain better resolution than with magnitude-only data.

, by combining the $\ell _2$-norm with the total variation of magnitude, the proposed approach can be used to reconstruct complex-valued reflectivities from undersampled data, and that the ADMM framework provides a flexible framework that can be used for other applications, such as multi-channel imaging.
